# FILE: docs/delivery/DESKTOP.md

# Desktop, Maiden and optional container delivery

Authorized 2026-09-08; supplements AUDIO.md and overrides historical MIDI-only
scope. Implementation is authorized after concrete card preparation and the
local review checkpoints. WSL Ubuntu 20.04 remains the primary working path.
This queue supplements the active Mosaic audio/device and broader script goal.

Stage 1 and stage 2 are now reviewed and merged through `1ec7174`. H00 source
inspection, concrete architecture choices, dependency findings and automated
acceptance are recorded in [H00.md](completions/H00.md), with immutable file
identities in [references/H00.json](references/H00.json). That contract refines
the cards below; implementation awaits its bounded plan review.

## Ownership and existing evidence

Worktree inspection: main at 319e3a0 owns the Mosaic campaign; audio-monitor at
319e3a0 owns audio/device work; codex/midi-hotplug at 859b8b5 and detached Linux
validation at bdf97b6 also exist. Recheck status before cross-cutting edits.
Preserve their work and the existing browser demo. This worktree records progress
in audio-state.json; do not overwrite the concurrent main state.json campaign.

Existing A00/A01 evidence covers real norns/JACK/SC synthesis and WAV capture,
external engines and one n.b. player, plus browser PCM rendering. These are
experimental scoped results, not proof of direct host output or all engines.
Reuse launcher isolation, browser controls/framebuffer/grid, MIDI and automation.

## Cards and dependencies

| Card | Missing capability and smallest integration | Automated acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| H00 reference audit | Inspect winder/norns-dev and schollz/norns-desktop Dockerfiles, services, startup, audio routing/streaming and runtime diffs at recorded commits. Check official upstream for existing fixes. Record licences before copying any code. | Reproducible inspected commits/file inventory, patch comparison and attribution decisions. Repository claims are hypotheses, especially external-device support. |
| H01 direct desktop audio | After H00, add an opt-in owned route from existing JACK output to the available WSL/Windows audio sink. Reuse real official norns/SC, existing capture and lifecycle. | Generic supported engine, measured frequency/RMS and routing; sink-boundary capture where available; start/stop/restart, isolation, missing-sink failure and cleanup. Distinguish engine, transport, browser and audible host boundaries. Manual listening is not a gate. |
| H02 official Maiden | After H00, pin official Maiden and integrate its editor/REPL with launcher-owned sessions, ports and lifecycle; disposable editable project only. | Browser automation edits and runs a generic script; changed runtime output and REPL reply; two-session switching/restart, data/project isolation and cleanup. Never overwrite user projects. |
| H03 portable browser audio | After H01 routing assessment, extend existing PCM/worklet path only where needed. Avoid a second controls/screen implementation. | Actual runtime signal at browser renderer; disconnect/reconnect, stale-stream rejection, cleanup and measured end-to-end latency. State monitoring versus interactive suitability from measurement. |
| H04 optional Docker baseline | After H00 and launcher contract audit, build pinned official sources and reuse existing launcher/browser/automation. Editable host code mount, persistent data mount, owned processes. WSL path remains available. | Container generic script startup, browser controls, virtual grid, exact MIDI capture, editable code reload, data persistence, restart and cleanup. Pin image/build inputs and record host/container architecture. |
| H05 platform matrix | After H04, validate Windows and macOS separately, Apple Silicon where available. Investigate H03 browser route for portable output. | Per-host startup/control/grid/MIDI/audio/latency/mount/cleanup evidence. Linux-only container success cannot admit Windows/macOS. Unavailable host remains not_run, with reproducible runner instructions. Document physical USB/MIDI/grid/audio limitations individually. |

User queue correction, 2026-09-08: all H00-H05 work follows completion of reliable
Mosaic audio/device capabilities (including audible-click investigation), then
broader script support such as cheat codes 2. Do not switch after only the Crow
ii checkpoint. Within this later tranche, priority is H01, H02, then H03;
H04/H05 are optional distribution work, not a replacement runtime. Preparatory
queue documentation is not permission to bypass the earlier tranche.

H00 must populate for each priority: existing evidence, concrete capability gap,
adaptable architecture/configuration, smallest session-compatible implementation,
and actual-feature test. Review this expansion with the runbook's Codex Paranoia
medium/10-minute budget, one critique plus focused follow-up. Review integration
at admission using the same budget; no mandatory human/hardware certification.

## Source and licensing boundary

References: https://github.com/winder/norns-dev and
https://github.com/schollz/norns-desktop. H00 records the inspected source commits
and file inventory. Winder declares GPL-3.0: architectural ideas may inform
independent integration, but no source is copied into this MIT project without
an explicit compatible licensing decision and attribution. No repository licence
was found for Schollz's reference, so no source is copied. Keep official monome runtime pins. Any required borrowed runtime
change is an explicit patch with official base, rationale and removal condition.

Deliver working eligible features, automated evidence, user instructions,
reference/attribution notes and exact limitations. This document is a queue and
acceptance contract, not evidence of implementation or platform support.


# FILE: docs/delivery/completions/H00.md

# H00 architecture audit and implementation contract

2026-09-08, after stage 2 merged at `1ec7174`. Source and read-only host
inspection is complete; feature implementation/acceptance below is not yet done.
File SHA256 inventories are in `../references/H00.json`. Reference checkouts
remain ignored at `.runtime/h00`; no reference implementation is copied into core.

## Inspected references

- [Winder norns-dev](https://github.com/winder/norns-dev/tree/a13ad4c2038184e093e9b1cbab234c7df23c059d),
  GPL-3.0. Its base is Debian 10.10 with separately built JACK/SC/libmonome;
  the test image pins official norns `740cbeed0fd4890f420d9fbc8691ccefbe73b5e4`
  and Maiden `1daf030c2c81b8d8fadadda22e1de5d1ec1381f1`, but uses a floating base
  image and floating script clones. tmuxp starts Xvfb, JACK, crone, matron and
  Maiden with sleeps. Dummy JACK is default; Linux audio instructions replace
  it with ALSA and pass `/dev/snd` plus the audio group. The README marks macOS
  unsupported. Adapt process topology only; keep our readiness checks, source
  pins, native framebuffer and virtual devices. No GPL source is copied.
- [Schollz norns-desktop](https://github.com/schollz/norns-desktop/tree/701f641b9285136c562892d9941452419ed131ef).
  No repository licence file was found; do not infer permission from its
  relationship to Winder. No source/assets/scripts will be copied. The Dockerfile
  uses Debian Bookworm, amd64 Go and community norns/Maiden forks; startup uses
  fixed ports, sleeps, Xvfb, an image-capture server and ws-wrapper. JACK feeds
  DarkIce then Icecast MP3 (`bufferSecs=1`), with Caddy routing the editor/REPL
  and stream. That suggests a portable monitoring route, not low-latency proof.
  Its README first excludes external grid/MIDI/audio input, then gives grid
  and ALSA instructions; those claims are inconsistent, not host acceptance.
  Restart scripts kill processes by broad name matching. We retain owned PIDs,
  per-session ports/data, current controls and existing PCM/worklet playback.
- [Official Maiden](https://github.com/monome/maiden/tree/2e64f7d59284962ac68055dd556e3fd8515462f8),
  GPL-3.0. Proposed separate pinned runtime component, retaining licence and
  corresponding-source/distribution records; no re-licensing as MIT. Its server
  supports `--app`, `--data`, `--doc` and `--fd`; the latter accepts a launcher
  supplied loopback listener. Its web client reads `repl-endpoints.json`, uses
  WebSocket subprotocol `bus.sp.nanomsg.org`, newline for Lua and ESC for SC.
  Go and web dependencies have their own manifests; build tools/assets need
  pinned identities in the optional Maiden component bundle.

## Runtime/fork comparison

Inspected the exact reference norns fork
`8e72d2015e1a966c023834a24e6a6fbe998e2ce4`: its tip changes a font to Particle;
that is unrelated to our missing audio/editor capabilities and is not adopted.
The reference Dockerfile additionally rewrites tape disk and screensaver code;
those are not needed for this integration and are not copied.

Inspected Maiden fork `ce4471e25a45c87040817c0619f3596fa43060aa` and preceding
`f008c755a5c41c957b7f7fc60e9a443b8a1866fc`: systemd operations are replaced with
hardcoded restart scripts. Current official Maiden instead explicitly returns
503 when D-Bus is absent. Its `.sc`/`.scd` text MIME override is already upstream
(`cmd/server.go`, issue 219 comment). No fork patch is required for either.

Our pinned official norns `14bbeae8646c6717f6bb44c8cd60250bf94b6042` already has
stdin-driven matron execution and configurable service ports. Existing launcher
children have stdin pipes and owned output logs. Prefer a small WebSocket/stdio
adapter to these official interfaces. The official ws-wrapper is informative,
but returns zero after a child fails; blindly replacing our process ownership
with it would lose the strict exit checks. Do not do that. If implementation
reveals a necessary runtime patch, document its official base, rationale and
removal condition before adding it, and check official upstream first.

## Actual host observations

WSL Ubuntu 20.04 exposes `/mnt/wslg/PulseServer`. Read-only pactl inspection finds
PulseAudio 17.0-25-gc3305, `RDPSink` and `RDPSink.monitor`, stereo s16le 44100 Hz.
This is an available transport/sink to test, not proof that our runtime is audible.
The current emulator already has actual JACK/SC/engine PCM and browser-rendered
audio evidence, but no desktop sink-boundary acceptance.

Windows Docker client 20.10.17 is installed; its engine named pipe is absent.
The WSL Docker shim reports integration unavailable. No daemon or integration
setting was changed by this audit. Go is not in the WSL login PATH. These are
dependency findings, not platform failure claims. H04 can inspect/start the
installed Docker service when eligible or record an exact setup blocker; it
must not replace WSL or assert macOS support. No macOS host is currently present.

## Concrete scope, dependencies and acceptance

| Priority | Existing capability and missing user action | Smallest compatible addition | Automated actual-feature proof |
|---|---|---|---|
| H01 desktop audio | Native JACK/SC and bounded capture exist; users cannot select direct desktop output | Opt-in owned JACK-to-Pulse sink helper, real-time callback separated from blocking sink writes; explicit server/sink, per-session stream identity, no global daemon/default-sink changes. Add helper identity to a new candidate manifest while preserving the admitted candidate | Generic TestSine reaches selected WSLg sink monitor with frequency/RMS and silence controls. Inspect routing and sink-input identity. Attempt Windows output-loopback capture to test the later host boundary; report each boundary independently. Exercise start/stop/restart, two streams, missing sink, sink loss and owned cleanup. No manual listening or physical device prerequisite |
| H02 official Maiden | Editable external scripts, stdin-capable native processes and isolated dust exist; no editor/REPL UI | Separate optional official Maiden lock/build bundle. Per-session app configuration and loopback listener; same launcher opens its editor. Owned WebSocket relay to actual matron/SC stdin/output, preserving Lua/SC framing and logs. SC interactive mode must be probed. Route only owned lifecycle commands; never call host-wide systemd restart scripts | Browser edits a disposable Lua project, saves and runs it through Maiden; verify changed native screen/MIDI or captured engine output and actual Lua plus SC REPL replies/errors. Switch between two sessions and restart/reconnect; stale URLs/streams must not reach the other session. Check source/data isolation and complete process/port cleanup. No user project overwritten |
| H03 browser audio | Existing float PCM/worklet route, rate conversion and continuous tone checks exist; latency is unmeasured and long callbacks block audio reads | Preserve one browser/control implementation. Separate stream reads/lifetime locking from long device actions; retain bounded buffers, explicit gaps and stream generation checks. Add timestamps/clock-offset measurement only where necessary to measure real input-to-render latency | Real native stimulus at browser renderer, disconnect/reconnect/stale generation and cleanup. Long callback must not interrupt the stream. Measure latency distribution and uncertainty from actual native event/audio timing to rendering, both 44.1/48 kHz where available. Report suitability from measured results: interactive target p95 <=30 ms, monitoring target <=150 ms; higher results remain honestly labelled |
| H04 Docker | Official source builder and launcher/control/grid/MIDI contracts exist; no container distribution | New optional image built from pinned official sources and identified base/build inputs. Reuse launcher and native adapters. One container session exposes a fixed configurable HTTP port mapped to the same loopback host port; internal bind may be container-wide, ordinary WSL remains loopback. Mount editable code and persistent user data explicitly; own all child processes | Container generic startup, actual browser keys/encoders/frame, native virtual grid and exact MIDI bytes; edit/reload host-mounted script, save/restart persistent data, stop and prove cleanup. Record image digest, source/dependency identity, host/container architecture and mount ownership. Start without Mosaic/dependencies or physical USB |
| H05 host matrix | WSL/Windows browser path is tested; no Docker host matrix | Repeat container runner separately on available Windows and macOS hosts, including Apple Silicon where available. Browser route avoids assuming ALSA passthrough on a VM | Each host has its own startup/control/grid/MIDI/audio/latency/mount/restart/cleanup results. Missing hosts are `not_run` with reproducible instructions. Linux-only container evidence cannot admit Windows/macOS; list physical device limitations individually |

H01 precedes H02, then H03; H04/H05 follow as the optional distribution target.
H00 requires a bounded plan review before feature implementation, and integration
requires a separate bounded admission review. Each uses Codex medium, ten-minute
maximum, one review plus at most one focused follow-up per DESKTOP.md/RUNBOOK.
This contract does not promote defaults, add Mosaic requirements, rebuild screen
capture or treat reference configuration as proof that a feature works here.
request.stakes: Trusted single-user local general-purpose norns emulator. Audio and desktop support explicitly authorized. Existing real engine, browser, Crow subset and sampler/arc acceptance is merged; review only H00-H05 additions. Preserve official runtime, isolated data and processes, WSL path, honest automated audio boundaries and platform claims. No physical hardware certification or enterprise threat model.

content.text:
## What works

- `docs/delivery/completions/H00.md:81` requires “frequency/RMS and silence controls” at the selected sink monitor and reporting “each boundary independently.” This distinguishes desktop transport evidence from Windows output evidence.
- `docs/delivery/completions/H00.md:85` states “Missing hosts are `not_run`.” Unavailable macOS hardware therefore cannot produce a false platform pass.

## What doesn't work

- [MAJOR] **H02 omits an incompatibility between Maiden’s browser and the launcher’s directory mapping.** H00.md:82 proposes “Per-session app configuration and loopback listener” followed by browser editing. However, `src/runtime/native.py:103` creates application directories with `(dust/'code'/item.name).symlink_to(item,target_is_directory=True)`. Maiden’s `.runtime/h00/maiden/cmd/server.go:911–912` supplies directory children only for `if entry.IsDir()`, while `.runtime/h00/maiden/web/src/explorer.js:98–104` expands only `if (node.children)` and otherwise calls `bufferSelect(node.url)`. The launcher’s symlinked application directories consequently appear as files, blocking ordinary navigation to the script. **Contract invariant:** H02 must specify a compatible filesystem mapping or narrowly scoped adapter, and require browser navigation from the dust root through the actual launcher-created application directory before editing, saving and executing those same bytes; bypassing navigation cannot satisfy acceptance.

- [MAJOR] **H04 does not bind the implementation needed for persistent data reuse.** H00.md:84 says “Reuse launcher” and “Mount editable code and persistent user data explicitly,” with “save/restart persistent data” acceptance. Yet `src/automation/session.py:52,58–59` generates `session_id=uid()`, selects `data_path=Path(data).resolve()/session_id`, and creates it with `exist_ok=False`. Every new launch therefore receives fresh data even when the same host directory remains mounted; retaining old files alone does not restore the application. **Contract invariant:** H04 must define explicit reuse of an owned persistent dataset, separately from fresh-session isolation, including treatment of startup-generated system files. Acceptance must save through runtime inputs, terminate and recreate the container/session, then recover the saved behavior without test-only reseeding; failure must block persistence admission.

## Risks

- [MAJOR] **H02’s REPL error test can pass while leaving the emulator unusable.** H00.md:82 requires “actual Lua plus SC REPL replies/errors” but does not define subsequent recovery. `src/runtime/native.py:246–247` converts every SC log line beginning `ERROR:` into a retained `audio_engine_error`; line 264 then raises whenever `self.errors` is populated. A normal erroneous SC command therefore makes subsequent health checks and native controls fail, even after a corrected REPL command succeeds. **Contract invariant:** H02 must define recovery after interactive errors while preserving real engine-failure reporting. Require an erroneous command, its visible diagnostic, the declared recovery action, a successful command, and working browser controls/audio afterward; merely displaying the error is insufficient.

## Gaps

Nothing notable.

## Improvements

Nothing notable.
